items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Oscar Aleman the guitarist was a small built fellow... When George Carpentier spoke to Oscar... The pianist Jean Ferrier spoke... Oscar asked Jean... Oscar yelled out while we were playing a number

ctx.x: George Carpentier, the ex-heavy weight boxing champion, had a bar next door to the Villa d'Este and he came in the club every night. He always danced at least one a night when we played and he always spoke to each one of us as he danced by. Oscar Aleman the guitarist was a

small built fellow who was from Argentina and was very full of life. When George Carpentier spoke to Oscar, he always called him "little Monkey". George spoke English as well as I did whereas Oscar didn't know one word of English. But George had called him a little monkey so often that Oscar began to know the word and became suspicious about it being something unusual to call someone.

The pianist Jean Ferrier spoke and understood English not too bad, so one day Oscar asked Jean in French naturally what did the word monkey mean. Jean told him "un singe" which meant monkey in French. The next time that George Carpentier came in he was standing at the bar and Oscar was so impatient to let George know that he finally knew what a monkey was that he yelled out while we were playing a number: "Hellow George Carpentier, you big white monkey!"
